newsitem.title: UK: Concert caps BT's path from privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Concert caps BT's path from privatisation.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc shareholders on Tuesday approved its merger with MCI Communications Corp, sealing its transformation into a global telecoms force since its privatisation in 1984.
The $20 billion merger will form a combined Anglo-American company called Concert Plc.
Following are some of the key dates in its development:
1984 - Privatised under Margaret Thatcher's Conservative government. Issue helps to transform image of share ownership as millions of small investors buy into BT.
1985 - Faces first serious competitive challenge in the UK with the launch of Cable & Wireless Plc's Mercury Communications.
1985 - Launches Cellnet radio telephone in a joint venture with Securicor.
1988 - Acquires 22 percent of mobile phone company McCaw Cellular Communications Inc for $1.5 billion.
1991 - Government sells off remaining 48 pct British Telecommunications Plc (BT) stake.
1992 - BT wins licence from the German government to offer satellite services, adding to its existing satellite operations in France and the Netherlands.
1993 - Announces a multi-million pound, five-year contract to provide a communications network to improve Europe's air traffic management.
1993 - Pays $4.3 billion to take a 20 percent stake in MCI Communications Corp.
1993 - Joins forces with Banco Santander SA of Spain to sell a range of voice and data services.
1994 - Creates Concert Communications Co, a $1 billion joint venture with MCI to provide global corporate communciation services using IT technology.
1994 - Forms alliance with Danish, Finnish and Norwegian firms as part of push into Scandinavia.
1995 - Announces joint venture with Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro to target business customers.
March - Buys 25 percent stake in Clear Communications, New Zealand's second biggest telecoms company.
May - Breaks off merger talks with British rival Cable & Wireless Plc.
June - Announces 200 million stg investment in internet venture with MCI.
July - Forms computer networking and on-line services joint venture with Microsoft Corp.
Sept - Takes 25 percent stake in Cegetel, new French telecoms consortium led by Compagnie Generale des Eaux for 1.1 billion pounds and the share capital of BT France.
Oct - Enters Hungarian telecoms market; confirms intends to bid for Dutch telecom licence; says would seek a new telecoms partner in Germany after RWE AG quit alliance with BT and Viag.
Nov 3 - Confirms it will merge with MCI to create Concert Plc.
Nov 6 - BT-led group wins 10-year UK defence telecoms contract worth 700 million pounds.
Nov 13 - BT, MCI, and Microsoft expand their alliances to develop a range of global intranet services.
Dec 3 - MCI, BT file with U.S. Federal Communications Commission for merger approval.
Dec 13 - Swiss telecoms group Newtelco picks BT as one of its international strategic partners.
Jan 10 - BT to buy a 22.5 percent stake in India's Bharti Cellular Ltd.
Jan 17 - BT plays down top-level talks with Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp despite market speculation that the companies might hatch a deal.
Jan 30 - EU opens in-depth probe into BT-MCI merger.
Feb 4 - German government awards mobile telephone licence to group led by BT and Viag AG.
Feb 7 - Cable and Wireless Plc pulls out of partnership with Germany's Veba. BT and Veba later meet for talks, but play down speculation that the two might form an alliance.
Feb 17 - BT hails landmark World Trade Organisation international telecoms pact as "great news".
Feb 23 - BT and MCI say they want to keep MCI's stake in News Corp Ltd.
March 11 - BT and MCI form a global web hosting service to speed the flow of information over the Internet.
March 13 - BT and NTT join a group to bid for a Singapore basic telecoms services licence.
March 18 - BT forms a joint venture with Japan's Marubeni Corp to provide domestic and global communications services.
April 2 - MCI shareholders approve BT merger deal.
April 8 - BT prices $1.0 billion five-year bond.
April 14 - BT forms strategic alliance with Portugal Telecom, giving it access to South America's biggest market, Brazil.
BT declines to confirm Portugal Telecom's statement that MCI had struck a pan-American joint venture with Telefonica de Espana.
Telefonica denied a deal had been signed, and MCI in Lisbon said the statement had been released in error.
April 15 - BT shareholders overwhelmingly back its merger with MCI.
--Jeff Daeschner, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
